* fix(auth): validate bearer realm host to prevent credential exfiltration

attacker-controlled URL. Without validation, ORAS would send the user's
plaintext credentials or OAuth2 tokens to that arbitrary host.

any credential-bearing request. Add TrustedRealmHosts to Client for
deployments that legitimately use a separate token service host.

## Summary

Replaces the manual issue-vote → tag → release process with a PR-based
GitOps workflow.

## Changes

- **`.goreleaser.yaml`** — Minimal config for a Go library (no binary
builds, archives, or checksums). `prerelease: auto` marks tags
containing `-alpha`, `-beta`, or `-rc` as pre-release on GitHub.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — Triggers on merge of a
`release/vX.Y.Z` branch into `v2`. Extracts the version from the branch
name, tags the merge commit, and publishes the GitHub Release using the
PR body as release notes. The `goreleaser/goreleaser-action` is pinned
to `e435ccd` (v6.4.0).
- **`RELEASES.md`** — Documents the full release process, the
`--allow-empty` branch convention, and three levels of local testing
with `act`.
- **`.github/act/release-event.json`** — Mock PR event payload for local
workflow testing.

candidate_fix_commit.message:
Isolate TurnServer datagram and message processing from the receive loops (#1774)

A UDP datagram arriving on the TURN port is unauthenticated and arbitrary, and
the STUN parser throws on input it does not recognise. HandleUdpDatagram was
called inside the receive loop but outside any per datagram handler, with the
generic catch sitting outside the loop, so a throw unwound past the loop and
ended it. ReceiveUdpAsync is started fire and forget by Start() with no
supervision, so nothing restarted it: the UDP relay stayed down for every
client until the process was restarted.

Two ways in, both verified. A first byte with bits set that the STUN header
check rejects and which is not channel data throws ApplicationException from
STUNHeader.ParseSTUNHeader. A datagram too short to hold a STUN header but
starting with an accepted first byte gets a null header back from
ParseSTUNHeader, which STUNMessage.ParseSTUNMessage then dereferences for the
message length, throwing NullReferenceException

candidate_parent_commit.message:
Mark TurnServer experimental with diagnostic SIPSORCERY001 (#1773)

TurnServer is written for development, testing and small scale or embedded
scenarios, not for production. The XML documentation says so and lists the
limitations in detail, but a doc comment is easy to miss and carries no weight
at build time, so package consumers have had no real signal.

ExperimentalAttribute is the purpose built mechanism for this. Referencing
TurnServer is now a compile error until SIPSORCERY001 is suppressed, which
makes using it a deliberate decision rather than something discovered after
deployment. UrlFormat points the diagnostic at docs/diagnostics/SIPSORCERY001.md,
which spells out what is missing: no nonce validation or expiry, no rate
limiting or per-IP allocation caps, no TLS/DTLS on the control channel,
uncapped allocation lifetimes, UDP only relay, IPv4 only.

The attribute comes from the Polyfill package already referenced, so it applies
across all nine target frameworks including net46

fix: prevent arbitrary file upload in markdown editor (#12)

The attachments handler previously called $file->store() with no
validation, allowing any authenticated user to upload HTML, SVG, JS,
PHP or other executable files to the configured disk. When the disk
was a public cloud bucket, uploaded files were served with guessed
Content-Type, enabling stored XSS, phishing hosting, and malware
distribution on the application's storage domain.

- Enforce strict validation (file, image, mimes, extensions, max) on
  attachments before any store call
- Store uploads under a random filename with a server-side-derived
  extension instead of the client-provided name
- Sanitize the original filename before inserting it in the markdown
  output to prevent markdown/link breakout via crafted names
- Introduce an upload config section (max_size, allowed_extensions,
  images_only) so consumers can opt in to non-image types explicitly
- Derive the input accept attribute from config instead of hard-cod

fix(langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb): validate configurable checkpoint IDs (#2397)

## Summary

Fixes #2351

This change hardens `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb` against
object-based configurable input in checkpoint identifiers. It adds
runtime validation for `thread_id`, `checkpoint_ns`, and `checkpoint_id`
before any MongoDB query/write path uses these values, so operator-like
payloads are rejected early with explicit errors.

## Changes

### `@langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb`

- Added a shared `getStringConfigValue` runtime validator in
[`libs/checkpoint-mongodb/src/checkpoint.ts`](libs/checkpoint-mongodb/src/checkpoint.ts).
- Applied validation to `getTuple`, `list`, `put`, `putWrites`, and
`deleteThread`.
- Preserved existing behavior where `getTuple` returns `undefined` when
`thread_id` is missing, while now rejecting non-string values.
- Added regression tests in
[`libs/checkpoint-mongodb/src/tests/checkpoints.test.ts`](libs/checkpoint-mongodb/src/tests/checkpoints.

candidate_fix_commit.message:
fix(api): Fixed SSRF via Lunch Flow onboarding (#3122)

* fix(api): Fixed SSRF via Lunch Flow onboarding

This fixes an issue where the Lunch Flow setup process could be used to
forge server side requests from the monetr server itself to servers that
were not intended to be accessed via monetr or perform other actions
over the private network that were not intended.

This patch resolves https://github.com/monetr/monetr/security/advisories/GHSA-29v9-frvh-c426
by enforcing an allowed API url list in the monetr configuration. This
list defaults to the known and trusted Lunch Flow API URL, so any users
self-hosting monetr and using the normal Lunch Flow API will not be
affected.

However if any users are using a custom API URL for Lunch Flow then you
will see warnings when monetr attempts to sync or pull data for those
lunch flow connections. Even if a lunch flow link has been established,
monetr will not make requests to that API URL unless it has been added
to the allowed URL list.
